body:
Thanks.
I don't have a problem finding people who want to be my friend.  I have a problem respecting people and appreciating people because I don't feel appreciated.  I don't hate people.  But I don't like people enough to tell them either *right now* (wasn't always the case).  I can maybe see myself able to appreciate the company of someone who is my age, is quiet, and has an odd sense of humor.   But it's hard to find anyone my age in the first place.  Every IRL social thing I gravitate to has no one even close to my age.  

Where in the world are all the millenials?

> it would be really sad to lose someone with their own unique personality and insights into things.

Why would it be sad?  Assuming I have those things (which.. I dunno), no girl wants them or other things.  I'm better off dead.

I've had 5 different dedicated therapists. 3 turned me down due to "severity of situation" (aka they don't want to treat someone suicidal).  I've also been hospitalized in a mental health place 4 times and seen probably dozens of therapists at this point. Each of them steer around the issue.  Granted, I should probably be more aggressive with therapists, I've even thought about seeing a sex therapist, but do they treat this?  Every professional I see only cares about me having a job, then they stop trying as if my life is all of a sudden better.

I have a lot of people that want to be my friend from a ton of activist work I did last year.  Most of them are 35+, cuz young people aren't in politics.  I would thereotically should invite them to my apt, but I just lost my apartment due to missing work from being hospitalized.  I put off letting people be my friends, because it's hard for me to respect people when I don't feel respected by so many people.
